sentences.text: The Regional Dispatch Center provides continuous intake, triage support, ambulance dispatch, and regional coordination for emergency medical requests across participating jurisdictions.
Its mandate is to translate reported emergencies into prioritized incidents and coordinate an appropriate response under approved clinical and jurisdictional protocols.
The Regional Dispatch Center is known operationally as Juniper and serves as the region’s primary dispatch and coordination point.
The service operates continuously and maintains a shared operational picture of incidents, available units, and known access constraints.
Call Taker Mara obtains essential incident details, confirms the reported location, and enters the request for assessment.
The Triage Supervisor reviews incident information, assigns or confirms priority, and directs cases requiring additional clinical review.
The Regional Medical Director establishes clinical triage policies and defines the limits of protocol-based decision making.
Dispatch personnel apply approved protocols and seek clinical guidance when a case falls outside their delegated authority.
The Shift Commander is the on-duty operational authority for dispatch-center coordination and service continuity.
The Shift Commander is known operationally as Sundial during regional coordination and command communications.
The Shift Commander resolves operational conflicts, sets response priorities during surges, and escalates decisions beyond the center’s authority to the appropriate jurisdictional leadership.
The Shift Commander does not replace the Regional Medical Director’s authority over clinical policy or a Paramedic Crew’s clinical judgment at the scene.
The Radio Coordinator manages operational radio traffic and maintains communications discipline on the Regional Radio Network.
The Regional Radio Network carries dispatch and coordination communications among authorized responders.
The Ambulance Coordination Platform supports a current view of incidents, unit assignments, and regional resource status.
The Computer Aided Dispatch Console is the primary workstation for incident entry, assessment, and dispatch operations.
A Paramedic Crew retains responsibility for immediate patient assessment and care within its professional scope and applicable protocols.
Ambulance Unit 417 is managed as part of the regional response pool when assigned to an incident.
The Hospital Liaison Desk coordinates operational awareness of receiving capacity and destination constraints.
The Emergency Department communicates receiving considerations through established regional coordination procedures.
Riverside Trauma Center is a designated destination whose availability and suitability are considered under regional protocols.
The North Gate Status Board and South Gate Status Board provide visible status information relevant to access and movement planning.
The Fleet Maintenance Cell provides operational awareness of vehicle serviceability and maintenance constraints.
The Data Quality Officer reviews dispatch records for completeness, consistency, and compliance with applicable information-handling rules.
Participating jurisdictions retain ownership of their resources and remain responsible for local policy, while the regional service coordinates agreed response activity.
